chunks: The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) informed me, from Abū al-Qāsim Ja'far ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ya'qūb, from 'Alī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī 'Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abū 'Abd Allāh (peace be upon him)
who said: "Do not fumigate the shroud [with incense]."

key_terms.الْكَفَنَ: the funeral shroud; the cloth(s) used to wrap the deceased before burial
key_terms.تُجَمِّرِ: to fumigate or perfume with incense (from مِجْمَر, an incense brazier); the act of passing cloth over burning incense to scent it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia Islam to fumigate or perfume the funeral shroud with incense before burial?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) issues a prohibition against fumigating the funeral shroud (kafan) with incense. This terse legal ruling (ḥukm fiqhī) concerns the preparation of the deceased (tajhīz al-mayyit) and is transmitted through an authoritative chain including al-Kulaynī, al-Mufīd, and Ibn Abī 'Umayr. Al-Ṭūsī records it as the opening ḥadīth of the chapter on this question, indicating it represents the primary Imami ruling against this practice.
